passages.text:
When Simon heard this, he said, “You will not pressure me into keeping silent about his essence and investigating only his purpose. For it is possible both to think and to speak about his essence—I mean, starting from the good qualities belonging to human beings. For example, being alive and being dead belong to a human being, but to God belongs not being dead, but being alive—and being alive eternally. Again, human beings can be evil or good, but to God belongs being incomparably good. And, so that I may not prolong the argument at length, the better of the qualities belonging to human beings belong eternally to God.”

Peter said, “Tell me, Simon: does it belong to human beings to beget evil and good people and to do evil and good things?”

Simon said, “It does.”

Peter said, “Since you have spoken this way, the better of the qualities belonging to human beings must be assigned to God. Since human beings beget evil and good people, God can beget only good people; and since human beings do evil and good things, he himself delights in doing only good things. Thus, concerning God, either it is possible not to speak of the qualities belonging to human beings and to remain silent, or it is reasonable to assign to him the better of the good qualities belonging to human beings. In this way, he alone is the cause of all good things.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Οὐ δυσωπήσεις με περὶ τῆς οὐσίας αὐτοῦ σιωπή[σαν]τα περὶ τῆς προαιρέσεως αὐτοῦ [ζη]τεῖν μόνης.
lexical_decisions.chosen: You will not pressure me into keeping silent about his essence and investigating only his purpose.
lexical_decisions.rationale: The future with οὐ is taken as Simon’s negative declaration of refusal, fitting his ensuing claim that God’s essence can be discussed. The aorist participle σιωπήσαντα is rendered as attendant action coordinated in English with ζητεῖν. A temporally stricter alternative is “You will not pressure me, after I have kept silent about his essence, to investigate only his purpose,” while interrogative punctuation is grammatically possible but less suitable to the argumentative context.
οὐσία denotes God’s being or essence here, whereas the plural οὐσίαι in the next section denotes elemental substances.
The perfect infinitive τεθνάναι denotes the state of having died or being dead, not merely the process of dying.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the better of the qualities belonging to human beings
lexical_decisions.rationale: προσόντα denotes attributes or qualities that belong to someone, and κρείττονα selects those regarded as superior.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ δὲ θεῷ τὸ ἀσυγκρίτῳ ἀγαθῷ εἶναι
lexical_decisions.chosen: to God belongs being incomparably good
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀσυγκρίτῳ may describe the good as incomparable or convey the adverbial sense “incomparably”; the latter produces natural English without changing the claim.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὕτως π[ερὶ θεοῦ] ἢ οὐ τὰ ἀνθρώποις προσόντα λέγειν καὶ σιωπᾶν ἔστιν ἢ τῶν ἀνθρώποις προσόντων κα[λῶν] εὖλογόν ἐστιν ἀπονέμειν αὐτῷ τὰ κ[ρείτ]τονα
lexical_decisions.chosen: Thus, concerning God, either it is possible not to speak of the qualities belonging to human beings and to remain silent, or it is reasonable to assign to him the better of the good qualities belonging to human beings
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering lets ἔστιν govern the coordinated infinitives and takes οὐ directly with λέγειν. If οὐ is instead given wider scope, the first member could be read “it is not possible to speak of the qualities belonging to human beings and remain silent,” but that produces a less fitting contrast with the second alternative.
